Quick note from our finance/ops team — we saw a sizable spike in token consumption for the month of May that pushed us well above our committed capacity. Our contract shows a committed monthly capacity of 600M tokens; our internal reports indicate ~1.45B tokens for May. That delta will create a sizable overage on the invoice.

Before we push this to procurement, can you:
- confirm your records for May (raw usage by day)
- provide a reconciliation/one-time settlement amount you expect
- advise whether there are credits or contractual levers (rollover, cap adjustments) we can apply

We rely on Redwood for production ML inference and want to resolve this quickly — Victor (CC) is handling procurement and will need a number to present.

Thanks,

Kara / Victor — thanks for flagging. We've validated your May usage against our logs and attached a summarized export (usage_export_May2027.csv) showing daily tokens, peak 5-minute windows, and model families. Summary:

- Contracted monthly commit: 600,000,000 tokens
- Reported May consumption (Redwood verified): 1,448,732,914 tokens
- Delta (overage): 848,732,914 tokens
- Overage rate (per token): $0.000012 (per our published pricing table)
- Gross overage amount: $10,184.79

Recommended settlement options (pick one):
A) One-time invoice for gross overage = $10,184.79, plus a one-time goodwill credit of $2,000 applied to the next invoice (final due: $8,184.79).
B) Cap + amortize: bill 50% now ($5,092.40) and carry the remainder across June/July (split equally), no goodwill credit.
C) Contract amendment: if you expect persistent demand, convert to a higher committed tier (900M/month) retroactive to Jun 1 and apply a one-off top-up invoice to cover May overage at discounted rate (15% discount). Discount option requires an amendment and a 3-month minimum.

We've attached a short settlement memo (nebula_settlement_summary_May2027.pdf) with line items and the export. If you'd like, Laura can issue a formal invoice + DocuSign for option A or B.

Notes:
- We did not find evidence of duplicated requests or misrouting in the time window. A small portion (~2.1%) is attributable to a burst from an internal test environment on May 7 that your team reported; we've already excluded that in the numbers above.
- If Nebula wants an audit log (per-call IDs), we can pull detailed traces but that will take an extra 48 hours.

Next step: please confirm which option you prefer by EOD Friday so we can get paperwork out.

Thanks — Jordan
